SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Glucose and oxygen

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.

9. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.

13. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

14. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Removing all vegetation

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

5. A — Producers

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

8. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

9. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

10. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

13. A — newton (N)

14. B — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
